At home today, I spent a little too long last night trying to get the data we fill in at home to load once we launch the app on the work computer. This is starting to show signs that I’m getting very distracted from everything else I should be doing. I’ve put the project on hold until the morning trading session is done, because I’m starting to lose time from being too locked into the side project. That said, I think if we can get this part fixed, we’re pretty close to done for the most part other than seeing what we break over the next few weeks.

Our CVE trade is starting to erode on its EV, and I’m at a point where I’m not sure if we should keep pushing in on it. The climate for the play is shifting, and Trump’s bullshit is no longer pushing oil prices all over the place. That said, we do have more headlines this morning about a few ships being seized by Iran. Let’s keep this on watch, but keep in mind the trade has shifted for the last 3 days.

Heading into the office today. It’s just me, since Lars is in the neither lands.
The worst thing happened this morning. I went to put my headphones in to meditate on the train and the right earpiece was missing.

There are two possibilities: it popped out when I dropped them on the floor over the weekend, or it fell out when I was putting them away on the train on Thursday. If it’s the second one, we will need to get new headphones.
Let’s put some time into the mental game of trading slides for Monday and get a post written for it.

New day of the week, let’s crush it. Headlines are about oil, just like we expected. We’ve seen this pattern repeat every week since the war in Iran started. Let’s see if the market tanks again or if this gets shrugged off and we keep doing what we do, since this is now the 3rd or 4th time. I think we all know peace talks aren’t going to happen with Trump.

Feeling really good at where we have taken the trade engine. I think in another month we can take our subscription to the lower tier on Notion, let keep working on getting on month cost down on subscriptions

On today’s Zoom call, let’s dig a little deeper into the concept of playbooks working in different time periods—how to adjust, and what we mean when we say some playbooks work for a while and then stop. We’ll use a trend trade as an example, and also talk about the different size you need to see and how it trades differently depending on whether the market or sector is trending.

Got headshot on the Opening Drive trade. Everything looked good, XLE broke our key downside level, CL was looking weak, and we kept the 200 share size after chickening out the other day. Glad we took it with 200, but that being said, we got absolutely smoked, 12 cents in 12 seconds. The bid dropped right after we got in on the retest, then snapped the other way hard, exactly like we want to see when it works, just against us this time. XLE went from 55.80 back over 56.20 and we had to jam out.

Waited for the second leg trade since that has been setting up well too. We had clear resistance at 24.70, XLE was back under 56, and when resistance broke we got out quickly for a small 3 cent loss. Stayed hands off for 20 minutes after that.

Then JD gave us a setup, but we need to work on this stock more. Our level reads need work. We probably need to be posting passively 2 cents lower. This stock seems to like breaking support, pushing two levels down, pausing, then making higher highs. That is starting to become a noticeable pattern. Let’s see if we can start capitalizing on that.

At home today, we got news about the start: oil was down 10% in the premarket. I took the CVE trade and it printed, but we only took 100 since this play has not been hitting well on the bigger news days. Still, we locked in a nice 24 on that trade. I took two more attempts and gave back 6. That is when we flipped over to ERIC. It has meh earnings and has been getting spanked all morning. I traded it, but it is a very thick book and not necessarily something I trade when it is that thick.
Took a few closing imbalance trades. Maybe our theory of “under 5” isn’t as solid as we start getting a larger sample size.

Heading into the office today. I will be running the 11 call today since Lars will be in the air until a little later. Wayne is back, so there is no morning prep call.
Let’s dial back expectations on the CVE trade. It has not been giving us the go-go juice like it has the last few days.
One focus today: when punching into a position, pause and think before just jamming. See if you can get a re-bait on the way in, because fees right now are completely crushing us.

With Iran still in the background, headline risk is still quite high, but it feels like the market does not care anymore and is ready for the new story of the month.

Let’s be more cautious with our opening drive trade today. The markets have shifted, and I don’t think we’ll get the same movement we’ve been used to. Size down if you take it, and look for a quicker, smaller target. For today, let’s keep focusing on some of the TMS traders. Let’s reach out to the ones we think are going to make quick progress, and the next ones on their way to going live.

At home today, we used up all our Codex credits over the weekend. I think that if we want to keep making updates, we need to be more direct and stop asking the same thing over and over. The more detail we give, the less it uses.

New week. Let’s get our focus back. Last week put us in the negative for the week. The two-week ceasefire is mostly over, and the peace talks did not go well. Oil is back over 105 a barrel, so let’s see how we open and how the market unfolds.
GS will move the banking sector over 50, so we can’t trade it. Kicks off the banks earing lets highlight this on the call

At home this morning, I made good progress on the app, but we have run out of AI Go Go juice. We will have to wait until later today or next week to get a new reload. That said, we can work on a handful of other things. I am happy with where it is now, and I will work on an idea for the Ginger data dashboard to make the context of the data easier to read.

The opening drive was the right read this morning, but I wanted to let it come to my target. This is something I am only okay at, so I was working on it this morning. I was up 22 unrealized and let it come back to flat on the second half because I did not want to start taking small pieces off. We need to find a happy medium here somehow.

Heading into the office today, we hit closed orders yesterday. It was not the best day in a while, so let’s be more aware of how we are trading and stop pushing when that happens. If we miss our open trade, just chill and come back next session.
This morning was one of those odd mornings where I did not get up before the alarm, and it was a bit of a struggle getting out of bed.

It was a choppy read this morning. We did get a hit on the CVE trade, but ended up flat. We stopped out at -10 this morning because our reads were not as sharp, and things were not moving the way I want.

We got something new in the afternoon and jumped in to trade it. It took three stabs, and we stopped out on all of them. We had the right idea, but the risk was not tight enough. I am a little annoyed about it.

That said, my trade might not be there today, but let’s keep an open mind. This could still be a good short setup, since price has already moved 7% before the open.
Brutal day. After having a bigger day yesterday, we gave it all back and then some. We did size down, but our read was way off. Completely flipped.

Heading into the office today, let’s spend some time cleaning up our Notion and getting some templates going. It’s been a wild start to the morning. We’re all waiting on Trump’s deadline tonight at 8 PM. That said, Kaorg Island just got hit, so oil is starting to surge. We’ll be keeping an eye on this, especially after we got smoked yesterday on our opening drive play. I’m going to treat today with a lot more caution than normal.

We had one of our better starts so far this morning. I’ll add the tape to our playbook. We did chase price a little, because we didn’t punch right on time and we were still a little nervous it wasn’t going to go. Once XLE popped at 59.90 and started to build momentum, we got comfortable getting in. Once that trade was over, we flipped over to PFE as we were coming into the big 28 level we called out on the morning prep call. This was a little frustrating, because we only got a 4-share fill on the first trade, and then a 14-share fill on the second. I’m kind of thinking about trashing SUPR, as fill rate has been bunk over the last few weeks.ast few weeks

Took CCL into the close because it had a small buy imbalance. It was a mediocre trade. We made a little, but it did not move the way we thought it would. Other than that, the close was slow. The market was in a wait-and-see mode for the next four hours.

It’s a long weekend and I’m home solo, so I’ve got a solid chunk of time to tackle a few projects we’ve been putting off. The timeline is getting a lot closer. I’m using the tagging agent, and on May 4th it switches to a token-based system. It would cost about 70 bucks a month to run a simple file compiler. That pricing is insane. If it were an extra 10 a month, I’d pay for the convenience, but at these prices it feels like highway robbery. I’ll just build something with Claude.

Quick thought on automation: can we add a 150k shares task in the trader project? Also, in our mentor email update, can we get a notification once a trader reaches that goal so we can mark it as completed when they get close to going live?

Monday morning, our MPP is back to 0, and we’ve got a bunch of red days to knock off. Today’s goal is to lose less than 10 bucks or so. Let’s take the opening trade with caution. The markets are a little wild with all the Trump news and the moving deadline that’s now imposed for tomorrow at 8 PM. Oil pulled back from 120 on the 4 AM open to 110, and SPY and QQQ are starting to stop bleeding. I think we’re 50/50 on whether we get a taco or if he blows up the power plants. This is a wait-and-see day, and I think it’ll be extremely headline-driven.

We hit a closed order in 12 minutes yesterday. I think that’s a record, and it’s definitely one we want to avoid trying to beat. We’re lucky our MPP didn’t get distorted by it. Let’s lock in. Oil is back in play after Trump’s news conference last night, whatever you want to call it. It felt like he was pissed that the rocket was getting more headlines than him, and nothing new came out of the conference. Today, let’s stick to the plan: A setups only. Keep doing what you’ve been doing. One bad day doesn’t set the tone.

The CVE trade stepped up this morning. It was a very long six minutes, but it hit. Let’s size up again next week, and keep an eye on the headlines on Monday. I made a joke with Lar that maybe sub-2 dollar stocks on the imbalance numbers might be the thing. I’ve hit two for two. Let’s buckle in. We have to stop burning money. It feels like this week will be basically flat, two weeks in a row, after being down about one third of the daily risk limit the week before. Let’s keep doing what we’ve been doing and keep working on our back end.
